question: How many federal units will Fiocruz's InfoGripe SE 44 bulletin (released 12 November 2026) flag with SRAG incidence at alert level or above and a rising long-term trend?

calls.reasoning: Recent 2026 counts SE39-42: 3,1,3,5; SE44 2025 count was 3 (same seasonal window). Forecast horizon is two bulletins ahead (SE43 not yet public as of Nov 2). Rhinovirus/metapneumovirus circulation and national short-term increase at SE42 support counts staying in the 3-6 range; spring low influenza and frequent churn of states in/out of growth argue for mean reversion toward ~3. Median 4, right-skewed tail. No prediction market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers.

- Metric history 2026 (from question background / Fiocruz news): SE39=3 (AL, RR, SE); SE40=1 (SE; 6 more UFs at alert without growth: MA, MT, MS, RS, RR, SC); SE41=3 (GO, MT, SE); SE42=5 (AP, MA, MT, MS, SE; RR, SC at alert without growth). Published 29 Oct 2026.

- SE42 virology (last 4 weeks of positives): rhinovirus 53.3%, RSV 11.5%, SARS-CoV-2 6.4%, flu A 4.1%, flu B 5.4%.

- Resolves off the SE44 2026 Resumo PDF (data through 7 Nov 2026, pub 12 Nov) national-situation bullet 'N das 27 unidades federativas...'; stated total prevails over the count of named units.
- Event window: single bulletin SE44 published ~12 Nov 2026; as of 2 Nov 2026 the data week (1–7 Nov) has not started (0% elapsed).
- Searched but not found: the SE43 2026 bulletin (not yet published); readable text of the SE42 PDF; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold).

calls.reasoning: The 2026 weekly series for this metric was 3, 1, 3, 5 (SE39 to SE42), and SE44 2025 was 3. SE42 showed a slight national 3-week increase, SARS-CoV-2 rising in MT and MS, and metapneumovirus spreading in SE, MS, the Centre-South and the Northeast. That favours the count holding around 4-5, but this metric is volatile (states move between buckets weekly, e.g. RR and SC sit at alert without growth). SE43 had not been published as of this run. No market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers. Median 4, slightly below the last value of 5 to allow for reversion.

calls.reasoning: Anchor: the recent 2026 series (3,1,3,5) plus the 2025 SE44/SE45 values (3,3) puts the late-spring norm around 3. Status quo is SE42 = 5 (AP, MA, MT, MS, SE), which is high for the season. Fiocruz reports metapneumovirus cases declining and the national six-week trend only stable/oscillating, which argues for drift back toward 2-4. The three-week national trend was rising, COVID-19 was ticking up, and RR and SC were at alert without growth, all of which could add units. SE43 (published 5 Nov) was not available for this run. No human market was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. Median ~4, right-skewed.

calls.reasoning: The 2026 series for SE39-42 was 3, 1, 3, 5. The same week in 2025 (SE44 2025) was 3, as was SE45 2025. The latest value, 5, is high for late spring. Influenza is low and metapneumovirus may be fading nationally, which suggests reversion toward 3. Against that, SE42 showed a rising national 3-week trend, SARS-CoV-2 ticking up in MT and MS, and RR and SC sitting at alert without growth; any of these could hold the count at 4-6 or push it higher. SE43 is unavailable. No market was found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same evidence and land on a median of about 4. The SE40 figure (1 vs 3) was settled at 1 using the verbatim background text. Whether metapneumovirus was rising or declining nationally could not be settled without web access. Both regional rises and a national decline are plausible, so it is treated as two-sided. On the main judgment, partial reversion from 5 toward the seasonal norm of 3, I take a median of 4 with a right tail out to 7. I agree with Run 1's reference class and dispersion and carry them forward. I retrieved nothing new on this run, and I found no prediction market.
